body: @fxn @jeremy do you remember the reason? That test was added at https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/986cac73e3c56b3dfa22fd1464f6913e38d32cc3 and the `String` check at https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9de83050d3a4b260d4aeb5d09ec4eb64f913ba64.

I don't remember. That condition was added in [this commit](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9de83050d3a4b260d4aeb5d09ec4eb64f913ba64), let's summon @wycats and @carllerche in case they remember the good old days!

There's no feedback so let's try to do something that makes sense.

The original `capture` returned

``` ruby
buffer.presence || value
```

and [the patch that added the string type check](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9de83050d3a4b260d4aeb5d09ec4eb64f913ba64) introduced a conditional that changed the return value when it was not a string.

Then, in https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/986cac73e3c56b3dfa22fd1464f6913e38d32cc3 I added coverage for the method including that missed edge-case because I am better at a posteriori test coverage than a legion of TDDers :trollface:.

All in all, I believe `capture` should pass up the value as is if it is not a string, as it did before.

Sounds good to you guys?

:+1: 

> because I am better at a posteriori test coverage than a legion of TDDers :trollface:

:laughing:

I believe we had that check before to know when to build the `NonConcattingString`. That class was removed at Rails 3.1 and we should had removed the `is_a?(String)` check. That said, I agree with @fxn suggestion.

@carpodaster do you want to work in the patch?

@rafaelfranca but even if the `is_a?` check was needed in the original patch, it still changed the return value for values that were not strings, see what I mean? It could be the case that edge-case was an overlook.

issue.title: Re-enable capture'ing non-String values
issue.body:
This has been discussed in #17661 and partially reverts the changes made in 9de83050d3a4b260d4aeb5d09ec4eb64f913ba64 and 986cac73e3c56b3dfa22fd1464f6913e38d32cc3

The test case added to `content_for` acts as a regression / acceptance test.
